trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going up-right would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-left.
Going up-left would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going down-left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down-right.
The line must go left: up-right is number 17, which comes later; right is number 16, which comes later.
Going left would turn number 5 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.
Going right leaves no safe move afterwards; going up-right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down-right.
The line must go up-right: right is number 20, which comes later; down-right is number 19, which comes later.
Cell (0,-3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going right, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,-2). So the line goes down-right.
Going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,-3). So the line goes up-right.
Going down-right leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes right.
The line must go down-left: down-right is number 14, which comes later.
Going down-right would force the line onto number 14 before its turn. So the line goes down-left.
Going right would force the line onto number 14 before its turn; going down-left would force the line onto number 19 before its turn. So the line goes down-right.
Going up-right would force the line onto number 14 before its turn; going left would force the line onto number 19 before its turn (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes right.

Going up-right would leave both number 14 and cell (2,-1) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would cut off the top-right corner (3 cells) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes up-left.
Going right would turn number 14 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Going down-left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going left would cut off the middle (3 cells). So the line goes down-right.
The line must go down-left: left is number 18, which comes later.
Going up-right would turn number 18 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
